verdicts.reason: Re-read kb/rules.yaml CW-F06 (lines 597-620), CW-F04 (536-537), CW-F03, CW-R05 and PB-CW-WAITING step 4, plus FX1 in 54_fix_list.json. FX1 says to define 'during the wait' for waiting fees as the same window as CW-F04. For a waiting fee, CW-F04's window ends at FREE_WAIT_S (or boarding if earlier); E07's ends at 10:17:30. A1 instead runs CW-F06 to boarding. The credibility_note's reason ('a rider who reaches the pick-up ... before boarding does contest the fee') fails for waiting fees: every rider who boards reached the pick-up first. CW-R05 makes 'boarded after the free waiting period' the fee condition, and CW-F04 says what happens after the threshold does not count. I confirmed that the engine's proxy reads "I'm downstairs, where are you?" as PLACES (/tmp/a1check/skeptic/msgs.py: ESCALATE_HUMAN R7 HUMAN on V06). The card itself lists 'where are you?' as a STRONG example. So E07 plus that message at 10:20:50 gives STRONG, then CW-R12, then ESCALATE_HUMAN under A1, versus UPHOLD under FX1's window. That is an outcome change in CW-WAITING, an in-scope type. The message pattern is common: round 1 E08 has "I'm downstairs at the porch, don't see you?". D27 ('done') does not flag the departure. D30 states the window but asks only about messages sent before the arrival. The no-show end at the cancellation is defensible (a rider who arrives before the cancellation contests 'no show'), matches the v0.1 engine, and FX1 does not prescribe it. One nuance for the fix: a strict send-time cut at the threshold would drop a post-threshold message that describes presence during the free wait ("I've been here since 10:15"). So the test should be content placing the rider at the pick-up during CW-F04's window, not send time alone.

Reproduced in /tmp/a1check/skeptic/msgs.py (V06 plus one rider message at 08:47). "I'm waiting for the lift, 2 min" gives PLACES, STRONG, ESCALATE_HUMAN R7 HUMAN, because RIDER_PLACE_PHRASES[0] matches any "I'm waiting". "where r u" and "here already" give UNCLEAR, UPHOLD R8 APPROVE. "be there soon", "give me 2 min" and "ok thanks" give UNCLEAR, APPROVE. A paraphrase battery (/tmp/a1check/skeptic/battery.py) misread 17 of 36 plausible wordings: 2 false STRONG ("I'm waiting for the lift", "I'm waiting for my friend") and 6 placing or contesting messages read as UNCLEAR ("Where are u?", "I've been here for 5 minutes", "which side are you at?"). I raised the severity from MAJOR. The rule card itself is right, but validation plan step V4.4 makes this engine the KB decider for no-show cases. Round 1 scored those cases by engine output (51_scorecard by_decider engine 2/4) and graded the E01/E03 engine mismatches CRITICAL, and round 2 reuses the same tools. A false STRONG (ESCALATE instead of UPHOLD) or a missed placing message (UPHOLD instead of ESCALATE) therefore changes an outcome in CW-NOSHOW, an in-scope type. If the owner counts only the rule card's behavior (LLM reading at run time), this drops to MAJOR.

The engine counts rider GPS from `anchor` but rider calls and messages from `t_arr` (engine_noshow.py, the CW-F05 and CW-F06 blocks around lines 628-660). CW-F06 now defines the window from the arrival indication for all sources. Reproduced in /tmp/a1check/skeptic/adv.py (ryde_2026 advance booking, scheduled 08:45, arrival 08:38, non-contesting ticket). Rider GPS at the pin at 08:40, 08:42 and 08:44 gives UPHOLD R8 AUTO with F-RIDER-EVIDENCE NONE. Rider GPS at 08:46 and 08:48 gives STRONG, R7. The message "I'm at the pick-up point, where are you?" at 08:42 gives STRONG, ESCALATE_HUMAN R7. So the card and the engine disagree, and A1 made the card explicit. The engine split predates A1. MAJOR is right: no round 1 case and no organizer source (DISP-002, handbook) has rider_gps_telemetry, so this is outcome-neutral in the current scope. Which side should change is also an owner judgment (like D30): rider GPS that ends before the scheduled time is weak evidence against a no-show.

verdicts.reason: I re-read kb/rules.yaml lines 591-622. CW-F06 now reads 'During the wait means from the driver's arrival indication ... to the cancellation for a no-show fee, or to boarding for a waiting fee', and the zh says the same. FX1 in 54_fix_list.json says 'define during the wait for waiting fees (same window as CW-F04)', and CW-F04 (line 530ff) ends its window at the threshold. CW-R05 and RYDE-23534478435353 make the fee depend on boarding after more than 3 minutes. Every rider reaches the pick-up before boarding, so the credibility_note's reason ('a rider who reaches the pick-up ... before boarding, does contest the fee') is false for waiting fees. I ran the engine proxy in /tmp/a1check/proxy.py: rider_contact_reading returns PLACES for both "I'm downstairs, where are you?" and "I'm here". Under the rule text, E07 (free wait expired 10:17:30, boarded 10:21:10) plus 'I'm here' at 10:20:50 is a message inside the window that places the rider at the pin. That makes it STRONG, so CW-R12 gives ESCALATE_HUMAN (tier HUMAN). With CW-F04's window the message falls outside and the fee is upheld. Rider GPS works the same way: within 50 m before boarding gives STRONG. Two facts mean nothing tests this window. The engine cannot run waiting fees at all: line 338 sets end = T(t['cancellation_time']), which is null for E07. And V58 is built on the no-show base V06 (clean(), cancellation at 08:52). E07 itself is not affected, because its 'coming down' message reads LATE. In E08 the message falls inside CW-F04's window anyway. The defect still changes outcome and tier for a routine pattern in CW-WAITING, which taxonomy scope lists as ADJUDICATE. For no-show fees, ending at the cancellation is defensible. For waiting fees, ending at boarding is not.

FC-R03 (rules.yaml ~1003-1031) keeps credibility C. Its new statement excludes METERED fares 'as CW-R00 excludes RydeTAXI from the cancellation policy', which is an analogy. None of the three added Ryde quotes says detour refunds are excluded for RydeTAXI, so the exclusion is FairRyde's extension. credibility_principle (line 41) rates that D. There is no FAIRRYDE source citing D28, unlike CW-F03B, which cites D26. The source note calls RYDE-30741244296217 the 'Basis of the METERED exclusion'. The corpus shows that article is 'I was overcharged for ERP/toll', in Fares and Charges, edited 2025-07-17, which is B. check_report.md row 219 and META-04 'Fare basis' (rules.yaml ~154) show its quote is one side of a known conflict. The credibility_note's statement that the exclusion 'rests on Ryde's RydeTAXI articles (edited 2026-01-26)' contradicts that source note. The note also says the exclusion 'never decides an outcome on its own'. 44_comparison.jsonl shows E10 went from PARTIAL_REFUND S$9.60 at APPROVE in v0.1 to ESCALATE_HUMAN, and the exclusion alone made that change. The tier is unaffected (ESCALATE_HUMAN is always HUMAN, and C and D rows are both decisive), so the rating is wrong but outcome-neutral, which is MAJOR. One detail does not hold: explain.py has no FC-ROUTE explainer (only noshow), so the claimed _rule_label effect cannot happen today.

FC-R03 says 'Ryde's texts leave taxi fares to the taxi company and give no basis for a refund computed by the platform', and the zh says '把出租车车费交给出租车公司'. The corpus has RYDE-900003406966: fees 'follow that of the respective taxi company', 'The actual charges vary among different taxi companies', and the cash-only sentence. A corpus search shows taxi-company contacts only in the lost-item articles (900003102263, 25969395777305). No Ryde text names the taxi company as the handler of fare complaints. FC-R05's only source is a DiDi paraphrase (INDUSTRY), so 'no basis for a platform-computed refund' is equally true of RECALCULATED fares and does not distinguish METERED. The real distinguishing facts are missing from the rule: the driver collects a cash fare, and ontology line 376 models Ryde as REFUND_DECIDER 'for charges Ryde collected'. The wording comes from the FX2 problem text, but the rule text is what appliers read. This is wording and missing detail with no outcome effect, so MINOR.

FC-R05 (lines ~1048-1063) lists TAXI_TARIFF as a parameter and now says that for METERED fares 'the same formula gives a difference that is attached for the reviewer as information'. In reference_data.yaml, TAXI_TARIFF is the ComfortDelGro page (credibility C), with the note 'which operator's meter applies per trip is not recorded'. RYDE-900003406966 says charges vary among taxi companies. FC-R05 gives the reviewer no caveat. The parameter predates A1, and the caveat exists only in the reference_data note. The figure is information only, so this is outcome-neutral. Missing detail, so MINOR.

46_human_check.jsonl records only case verdicts for E01, E03 and E07 (UPHOLD). The CW-F06 source note ('... cases E01, E03 and E07, confirmed by Jasper on 2026-10-11') is grammatically ambiguous, and D27 is marked 'decide: done' without mentioning the window end. D30 treats the window 'to the cancellation or boarding' as the default and leaves only messages before the arrival open. No open item records the choice between threshold and cancellation or boarding, although it departs from FX1's 'same window as CW-F04' and CW-F06 is D, which must be confirmed. This is a labeling and traceability gap, so MINOR.

The CW-F06 text says only 'a message that fits neither reading', and the zh says '两种读法都套不上'. The engine docstring and code (engine_noshow.py line 176ff) return UNCLEAR for 'neither list or both'. I ran the proxy: "I'm here, coming out now" returns UNCLEAR. Self-test V62 expects UPHOLD/APPROVE, and check_report shows it passes. The rule text has no precedence for a message that fits both readings, so an applier could rate it STRONG under the first clause, while the rule's 'judged by reading it' leaves room for either reading. The text and the engine diverge on wording, so MINOR.

In FC-R05, the English is 'recomputed on the recommended route with the same tariff, fee tiers and surcharges', and the zh is '按推荐路线、同一费率重算的车费', with no fee tiers or surcharges. The v0.1 zh was the same (the git diff shows only an appended sentence), so this predates A1, but A1 edited that zh line. Translation gap, so MINOR.

rules.yaml line 1004 still reads 'name: Unjustified detour on a metered or recalculated fare', while the statement now says METERED fares are excluded. The contradiction is real. The stated failure path is overstated, though: explain.py builds explanations only for no-shows, so _rule_label does not print FC-R03 today. The name is still a visible label in reports and to appliers. Labeling, so MINOR.

review.dimension: ADVERSARIAL TEST OF THE ENGINE CHANGE (kb/tools/engine_noshow.py rider_contact_reading, reading_test, CW-F06 window)
checked_ok: The new self-tests pass: selftest.py gives 70/70, and V56 to V64 all PASS with their expected outcome and tier.

The rule card's own examples are read correctly: 'I'm at the pick-up point', 'where are you?' and 'I can't see your car' are PLACES. The round 1 rider messages from E01, E03, E04 and E07 are read LATE. E02's four rider contacts read PLACES, PLACES, UNCLEAR (a call) and PLACES, so E02 stays STRONG.

The window edges match the card's inclusive window (arrival 08:43:00 to cancellation 08:52:00). 'I'm at the lobby, where are you?' at 08:43:00 or at 08:52:00 gives ESCALATE_HUMAN R7 HUMAN. The same message at 08:42:59 or 08:52:01 gives UPHOLD R8 AUTO.

Mixed sets behave as designed. LATE+PLACES gives STRONG, ESCALATE_HUMAN, HUMAN. LATE+UNCLEAR gives UPHOLD APPROVE with CW-F06 decisive. LATE+NEUTRAL gives UPHOLD AUTO. A rider call plus a LATE message gives UPHOLD APPROVE (the call is UNCLEAR and the reading test makes CW-F06 decisive). A missed rider call alone gives APPROVE. Rider contacts with type 'voice' or 'text' read UNCLEAR and give APPROVE, which is the safe direction.
The curly apostrophe U+2019 is normalized: 'I’m here', 'I’m at the lobby', 'can’t see you' and 'don’t see your car' all read PLACES.

Many Singapore English placements with no LATE token fall to UNCLEAR, and the reading test then makes CW-F06 decisive, giving APPROVE, never AUTO. This held for 'reach already', 'i downstairs liao', 'where u', 'u here?', 'at lobby now', 'I'm at the void deck', 'which car r u', 'ur car where', 'i see u le', 'cannot find', 'outside 7-11 waiting', 'Hello?', 'no car here leh', 'you haven't arrived' and 'u never come'. 'im here lah', 'I'm here', 'Im here', 'i'm outside' and 'waiting outside 7-11' read PLACES.

Real admissions read LATE: 'on the way', 'coming', 'Coming!', 'coming down now', 'so sorry, running late', 'walking over', 'still upstairs', 'almost there', 'can wait for me?', 'I'm still at home, sorry' and 'I'll be down in 3'. 'ok', 'okay', 'k', 'noted' and 'Thank you' read NEUTRAL. Weaker forms such as 'otw', 'abt to reach', 'wait ah', '5 min' and 'ok thanks' read UNCLEAR, which only costs an approval.

No new exception path. None content crashes earlier in intake (line 232, re.search on None, pre-existing). A contact without 'type' would already fail in the intake text loop. rider_contact_reading itself handles missing or None content. The worst regex case is 1.1 s on a 21,000-character message. The cid lookup by identity always resolves because rider_contacts comes from the same chat_logs list.
The literal sender == 'rider' match loses nothing: TX-ROLE's only alias for RIDER is 'rider', and every case file uses 'driver', 'rider' or 'system'.

Running the window to the cancellation instead of the CW-F04 threshold only moves no-show cases in the safe direction (V60: a placement after the threshold escalates). For CW-NOSHOW that is defensible, because a rider who reached the pick-up before the driver canceled has a real complaint.

The reading test is wired correctly. UNCLEAR ids trigger an evaluate with contact_reading='STRONG'. When that changes the outcome, decide_tier records CW-F06 as decisive (kind 'contact'), and GENERIC_ASSUMPTION_USED is set because CW-F06 is credibility D.

The repo was not modified. git status is clean apart from the ignored kb/tools/__pycache__, whose files all predate this check. Scratch scripts are in /tmp/a1check/ (harness.py, battery.py, unsafe.py, fullrun.py, edges.py, safedir.py).

findings.claim: When a rider asks the driver whether they are coming or on the way, the engine reads it as the rider admitting lateness (LATE). These questions contest the driver's marked arrival, but no reading test runs on LATE, so the fee is upheld automatically. The exclusion for driver-directed 'coming' only covers the two exact forms 'you coming' and 'u coming'. 'on the way', 'omw' and 'almost/nearly there' have no exclusion at all.
findings.evidence: RIDER_LATE_PHRASES = [r"(?<!you )(?<!u )\bcoming\b", r"\bon (my|the) way\b", r"\bomw\b", ... r"\b(almost|nearly) there\b", ...]; line 187: return "PLACES" if places and not late else ("LATE" if late and not places else "UNCLEAR"); reading_test only tests unclear_ids. Run output on baseline V06 (selftest.clean on KB().disp002), message at 08:47:00: 'driver coming?' ['LATE'] -> UPHOLD R8 tier=AUTO ev=WEAK decisive=[] | if PLACES: ESCALATE_HUMAN tier=HUMAN; same for 'uncle coming?', 'Uncle coming or not', 'Are you still coming?', 'Are you on the way?', 'u on the way?', 'Hello? Are you on the way?', 'Is anyone coming?', 'Are you almost there?', 'ur coming?', "you're coming?", 'youre coming or not', 'you all coming?', 'Your car coming?', 'u omw?' (all LATE -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO). With a non-contesting ticket the result is the same (ev=NONE, UPHOLD R8 AUTO).
findings.failure_scenario: The driver marks arrival at 08:43 and cancels at 08:52. During the wait the rider's only message is 'uncle coming?' or 'Are you on the way?'. This is the common Singapore way to tell a driver 'I don't see you', and the card counts 'where are you?' as STRONG. The engine reads it LATE, so F-RIDER-EVIDENCE is WEAK or NONE, the outcome is UPHOLD R8 and the tier is AUTO. The correct STRONG reading gives ESCALATE_HUMAN with tier HUMAN. When the same question follows a placement ('I'm here. Are you on the way?', 'I'm at the pick-up point. Driver still coming?'), the message reads UNCLEAR, and the engine proposes UPHOLD under APPROVE instead of the STRONG reading's ESCALATE_HUMAN.
findings.suggested_fix: Read 'coming', 'on the way', 'omw' and 'almost/nearly there' as LATE only when the subject is the rider ('I'm coming', 'coming down', 'on my way') or when there is no subject and no question. Read the question forms ('?', 'or not', 'anot') or a second or third person subject (you, u, ur, you're, uncle, driver, car, anyone, someone) as PLACES, or at least UNCLEAR. Add self-tests for 'uncle coming?', 'Are you on the way?' and 'I'm here. Are you on the way?'.

findings.claim: A rider who states their place in words outside the narrow PLACE list, and also asks the driver to wait, is read LATE, so the fee is upheld automatically. The LATE list contains polite wait requests ('pls wait', 'can wait', 'wait for me') that riders send from the pick-up. The PLACE list misses void deck, carpark, block or blk, 'reach' or 'reached', 'already there', and 'downstairs' or 'here' without 'I'm'. LATE wins whenever PLACES misses.
findings.evidence: RIDER_PLACE_PHRASES first pattern needs (i'?m|i am|we'?re|we are) + (here|outside|downstairs|waiting); the second needs 'i'm ... at' + (pick-?up|pin|lobby|entrance|porch|stand|gate|door|exit|kerb|curb). RIDER_LATE_PHRASES includes r"\bcan (you )?wait\b", r"\b(pls|please) wait\b", r"\bwait (for me|...)". Run output (baseline V06, 08:47:00): "I'm at the void deck, please wait" ['LATE'] -> UPHOLD R8 tier=AUTO | if PLACES: ESCALATE_HUMAN HUMAN; same LATE -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO for 'reached, pls wait', 'Reached the lobby, please wait', 'Already downstairs, please wait', 'downstairs already pls wait', "I'm already there, can you wait?", "Can you wait at the lobby? I'm already there", "I'm at the carpark, please wait", "I'm at Block 123, please wait", "I'm at the main road, please wait", 'at void deck, can wait?', 'here liao, can wait 1 min? i see your car'.
findings.failure_scenario: The driver is about to cancel, and the rider, standing at the HDB void deck pick-up, messages 'Uncle pls wait, I'm at the void deck already' or 'reach already, pls wait'. The message places the rider at the pick-up, and the card makes that STRONG (ESCALATE_HUMAN, tier HUMAN). The engine reads it LATE and gives UPHOLD R8 with tier AUTO. A rider who contested in the chat during the wait is auto-charged.
findings.suggested_fix: When a message has a LATE token and also any place or arrival token (reach, reached, here, there, already, downstairs, void deck, lobby, carpark, car park, blk, block, gate, stand, bus stop, entrance, outside), return UNCLEAR, never LATE, so the reading test runs. Keep bare polite wait requests ('pls wait', 'can wait') out of LATE unless they come with a first-person delay ('still', 'getting ready', 'N min', 'coming'). Extend PLACES with the Singapore place words and with 'reach' or 'reached' forms. Add self-tests for "I'm at the void deck, please wait" and 'reached, pls wait'.

findings.claim: The engine normalizes only the U+2019 apostrophe and needs 'i'?m' with no space. Other apostrophes common on phones and Chinese IMEs (U+2018, fullwidth U+FF07, backtick), 'I m' with a space and 'Iam' all miss every first-person PLACE pattern. Alone they read UNCLEAR, which is safe. With any LATE token they read LATE, giving AUTO.
findings.evidence: t = (c.get("content") or "").lower().replace("’", "'"). Run output (baseline V06, 08:47:00): 'I m here, pls wait' ['LATE'] -> UPHOLD R8 tier=AUTO | if PLACES: ESCALATE_HUMAN HUMAN; same for 'I‘m here, please wait' (U+2018), 'I＇m here, please wait' (U+FF07), 'Iam here pls wait', 'I m at the lobby, please wait'. Compare "I'm here" -> PLACES.
findings.failure_scenario: A rider types 'I m here, pls wait' (autocorrect split) or uses a Chinese keyboard's fullwidth apostrophe: 'I＇m here, please wait'. The engine reads LATE and gives UPHOLD R8 with tier AUTO. The straight-apostrophe version escalates.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize [‘’ʼ＇`´] to an apostrophe and collapse 'i m', 'iam' and 'im' to 'i'm' before matching. Add a self-test with a non-ASCII apostrophe plus 'please wait'.

findings.claim: The place-contest pattern needs 'wrong' before the noun, so a contest written the other way round ('the pin is wrong', 'my location is correct') is not PLACES. Combined with 'coming over' or 'pls wait', it reads LATE, giving AUTO.
findings.evidence: r"wrong (place|location|pin|spot|side|entrance)". Run output (baseline V06, 08:47:00): "the pin is wrong, I'm on the other side, coming over" ['LATE'] -> UPHOLD R8 tier=AUTO | if PLACES: ESCALATE_HUMAN HUMAN; 'my location is correct, pls wait' ['LATE'] -> UPHOLD R8 tier=AUTO | if PLACES: ESCALATE_HUMAN HUMAN.
findings.failure_scenario: The rider messages 'the pin is wrong, I'm on the other side, coming over'. That contests the place, which the card makes STRONG. The engine reads LATE and gives UPHOLD R8 with tier AUTO. CW-F07 can only catch it if the venue table happens to hold the place.
findings.suggested_fix: Also match (pin|location|place|address|side|entrance)\s+(is|was)\s+(wrong|correct|right) and 'other side'. Return UNCLEAR whenever a place-contest token appears together with a LATE token.

findings.claim: The acknowledgment list includes 'yes', 'yep', 'ya' and 'sure' and is read without the driver's preceding message. A 'yes' answering the driver's 'Are you at the lobby now?' places the rider, but it reads NEUTRAL. NEUTRAL contacts never get the reading test, so the fee is upheld automatically. The card only exempts an acknowledgment such as 'ok'.
findings.evidence: RIDER_ACK = r"\s*(ok(ay)?|k|thanks?( you)?|thx|noted|sure|alright|yes|yep|ya)\s*[.!]*\s*". Run output (baseline V06 plus driver message 'Are you at the lobby now?' at 08:46:30, rider reply at 08:47:00): 'yes' {'E-CHT-04': 'NEUTRAL'} -> UPHOLD R8 tier=AUTO ev=WEAK decisive=[]; same for 'ya', 'yep', 'Yes.', 'sure'.
findings.failure_scenario: The driver messages 'I'm at the lobby, are you here?' and the rider answers 'yes'. Then the driver cancels for no-show. The engine reads NEUTRAL and gives UPHOLD R8 with tier AUTO. Reading 'yes' as a placement gives ESCALATE_HUMAN.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep only ok, okay, k, noted, thanks and thx as NEUTRAL. Read 'yes', 'ya', 'yep' and 'sure' as UNCLEAR, so the reading test decides, or read them against the driver's last message when that is a location question.

findings.claim: The rule card now defines one window for all rider-side evidence ('from the driver's arrival indication (the wait anchor when there is none) to the cancellation'). The engine counts rider messages from the arrival indication (t_arr) but rider GPS from the anchor. In an advance booking the anchor is the later scheduled time, so the same placement counts when it is a message and not when it is a tier A GPS record.
findings.evidence: line 634: rider_contacts = [c for c in chat if c["sender"] == "rider" and t_arr <= T(c["timestamp"]) <= end]; line 652: if anchor <= T(g["timestamp"]) <= end: (rider GPS). Ryde advance booking (selftest._ryde_advance, arrival 08:38, scheduled 08:45, end 08:49:15, driver at the pin throughout): rider GPS at the pin at 08:40 -> UPHOLD R8 AUTO WEAK; rider message "I'm at the lobby, where are you?" at 08:40 -> ESCALATE_HUMAN R7 HUMAN STRONG.
findings.failure_scenario: Advance booking: the rider's phone GPS shows them at the pin at 08:40, after the driver's 08:38 arrival indication. By the card's new definition this is STRONG (ESCALATE_HUMAN). The engine ignores the ping and gives UPHOLD R8 with tier AUTO. The same fact as a chat message escalates.

findings.claim: Safe-direction misreading, but frequent. Two common admissions are read PLACES and escalated to a person, which brings back FX1's over-escalation of routine cases. verdicts.reason: I read kb/tools/engine_noshow.py lines 34 and 176-187. The lookbehind (?<!you )(?<!u ) only excludes 'you coming' and 'u coming'. 'on the way', 'omw' and 'almost/nearly there' have no driver-directed exclusion. LATE short-circuits: reading_test only runs on unclear_ids, so a LATE message never gets the other reading. I reproduced this with /tmp/a1check/probe.py (V06 = selftest.clean on KB().disp002, rider message at 08:47:00). 'driver coming?', 'uncle coming?', 'Are you on the way?', 'Are you still coming?', 'u omw?' and 'Are you almost there?' all read LATE and give UPHOLD R8, tier AUTO, no decisive rule (F-RIDER-EVIDENCE WEAK with the DISP-002 ticket, NONE with the non-contesting ticket). 'I'm here. Are you on the way?' and 'I'm at the pick-up point. Driver still coming?' read UNCLEAR and give UPHOLD R8 APPROVE, although 'I'm here' alone reads PLACES and gives ESCALATE_HUMAN R7 HUMAN. A question to the driver is not the rider admitting lateness. Under the card it is at least 'fits neither' (APPROVE), or STRONG like 'where are you?' (ESCALATE_HUMAN). The engine is the KB's decider for no-show cases in validation (README step V4.4, 43_kb_engine.jsonl), and FX1 asked for new held-out rider-message variants. So this changes the tier, and possibly the outcome, in CW-NOSHOW (scope ADJUDICATE).

I read RIDER_PLACE_PHRASES and RIDER_LATE_PHRASES (lines 28-38) and the combining line 187: PLACES only when no LATE token is present, and LATE whenever PLACES misses. I reproduced these on V06 at 08:47:00. "I'm at the void deck, please wait", 'reached, pls wait', 'Reached the lobby, please wait', 'Already downstairs, please wait', "I'm already there, can you wait?", "I'm at the carpark, please wait", "I'm at Block 123, please wait", 'here liao, can wait 1 min? i see your car', "Uncle pls wait, I'm at the void deck already" and 'reach already, pls wait' all read LATE, giving UPHOLD R8 AUTO (also with the non-contesting ticket). Without the wait request, "I'm at the void deck" and 'reached' read UNCLEAR (APPROVE). "I'm at the lobby, please wait" also reads UNCLEAR (APPROVE). So by the builder's own design these messages should at minimum be UNCLEAR and go to approval. The engine instead auto-upholds them. That is a tier change (AUTO instead of APPROVE or HUMAN) in an in-scope type.

Line 182 only replaces U+2019. I reproduced: 'I m here, pls wait', 'I‘m here, please wait' (U+2018), 'I＇m here, please wait' (U+FF07), 'Iam here pls wait' and 'I m at the lobby, please wait' read LATE, giving UPHOLD R8 AUTO. It does not; it goes to approval. Under the definitions, an AUTO-versus-APPROVE difference for the same content is still a tier change in CW-NOSHOW, so I rate it CRITICAL, not MAJOR. The root cause is the same as ENG-2 (a LATE token wins whenever the placement is missed). A fix for ENG-2 that returns UNCLEAR when a place token appears would cover most of this.

I reproduced: "the pin is wrong, I'm on the other side, coming over" and 'my location is correct, pls wait' read LATE, giving UPHOLD R8 AUTO. So the same content gets AUTO or APPROVE depending only on word order. Whether 'the pin is wrong' contests the place or admits the rider's own wrong pin is a judgment. But 'my location is correct, pls wait' plainly contests the place and should at least be UNCLEAR. That is a tier change in CW-NOSHOW, so CRITICAL under the definitions, not MAJOR.

RIDER_ACK (line 40) includes yes, yep, ya and sure, and is matched with re.fullmatch on the message alone, without the driver's preceding message. The finding's literal claim is true and on its own would be MINOR. V58 runs the no-show playbook on V06 (its label says E07 was a waiting fee, so it is not mislabeled). A rider always reaches the car before boarding, so the common pattern 'coming down, 2 min' followed by 'I'm downstairs' just before boarding is STRONG and escalates a routine late-rider waiting fee (UPHOLD changed to ESCALATE_HUMAN in CW-WAITING, scope ADJUDICATE). That brings FX1's over-escalation back for waiting fees. It contradicts FX1's required change ('same window as CW-F04'; CW-F04 ends at the threshold or at boarding, whichever comes first).
